message.content:
**Profitability deteriorated sharply over the most recent years (FY2021–FY2024), turning from large profits to large losses.**

Using the latest applicable annual disclosures (FY2024 10-K, accession 0001682852-25-000022, filed 2025-02-21; FY2023 10-K, accession 0001682852-24-000015), all figures in USD:

| Fiscal year (Dec 31) | Revenue | Operating income (loss) | Net income (loss) | Net margin | Operating margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2021 | $18.471B | $13.296B | $12.202B | 66.1% | 72.0% |
| 2022 | $19.263B | $9.420B | $8.362B | 43.4% | 48.9% |
| 2023 | $6.848B | $(4.239)B | $(4.714)B | (68.8)% | (61.9)% |
| 2024 | $3.236B | $(3.945)B | $(3.561)B | (110.0)% | (121.9)% |

Sources (financial_facts IDs): revenue 2606873/2606883/2606788/2606798; operating income 2604264/2604277/2604290/2604300; net income 2604093/2604106/2604119/2604129. Margins are my calculations (profit ÷ revenue on the same basis), not disclosed fields.

**What changed:**
- **2021→2022:** Profitability already declined — net income fell from $12.2B to $8.4B (−31%) and net margin from 66.1% to 43.4%, even though revenue rose slightly, as costs (e.g., R&D $1.99B→$3.30B) grew faster than sales.
- **2022→2023:** A collapse. Revenue fell 64% to $6.85B while operating expenses stayed high (R&D $4.85B, cost of sales $4.69B), producing a $4.71B net loss. The 10-K notes a $772M income tax provision in 2023 (including a valuation allowance) versus a benefit in 2024.
- **2023→2024:** The loss narrowed modestly — net loss improved $1.15B (24%) to $3.56B and operating loss improved $294M — because total operating expenses fell 35% ($11.09B→$7.18B: cost of sales −69%, SG&A −24%, R&D −6%). But revenue fell another 53% to $3.24B, so the net margin worsened to −110% (operating margin −122%). The 10-K attributes the revenue drop mainly to lower COVID vaccine sales volumes in Europe/rest-of-world as purchasing shifted from advance purchase agreements to a seasonal commercial market, plus lower U.S. vaccination rates and more competition (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:476800).

**Limitations:** The database snapshot ends with FY2024 annual data (plus 2025 quarterly facts, which are not annual and were not used). The company states product sales are *expected* to decline further in 2025 — that is a forward-looking statement, not a reported result. Margins are derived, and the FY2024 net margin is distorted by the small revenue base and a $46M tax benefit.
